Reference / plist/value

plist/value#

Immutable property-list values, independent from JSON and any wire format.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let value = PlistDictionary(
    PlistMember("enabled", PlistBoolean(true)),
    PlistMember("name", PlistString("Okkama")),
);
value.membership("enabled"); // true
value.print(recipient);      // one nominal members event

Description#

Immutable property-list values, independent from JSON and any wire format. Scalars retain their exact payloads: arbitrary signed int, finite float, exact Unicode string/bytes, Instant, and nonnegative int UID. No coercion, timezone conversion, reference resolution or serialization-specific narrowing.

print() emits exactly one typed event; the recipient chooses recursion and owns traversal/output limits. No reflection, casting, hidden I/O or JSON conversion. Repeated calls repeat the event; callback failures propagate. Container constructors never call child kind()/print(). Custom PlistValue implementations are accepted nominally, with their own behavior/lifetime.

Arrays/dictionaries snapshot size once, then ascending items once, borrowing their source without cursor/first/last/close calls. Negative maximum_items fails before source observation; negative/excess size fails before item reads. Default cardinality is 1024; zero accepts empty input. Source errors propagate and stop reads. Queries use retained snapshots, which can escape the source scope. No resource acquisition or destroy. Cardinality bounds references, not complete tree depth/bytes; scalar payload sizes remain caller-owned.

Dictionary members are ordered nominal entries rather than a native map. Names are exact strings, including empty; no trimming/case/Unicode folding. Duplicate detection is O(n²) after snapshot; lookup O(n), storage O(n). Duplicate/missing names have distinct typed errors retaining the exact name. XML/binary parsing and writing belong to later modules, not this model. Contract: docs/std/plist-value-guide.md. Run: okkama run -t std/plist/value.ok

object PlistDictionary#

object PlistDictionary does PlistValue

A dictionary reads like json (#141): text(name), int(name), float(name), boolean(name), data(name) for bytes, date(name) for an Instant, get(name) for a nested dictionary, dictionaries(name) for an array of them, texts(name) and ints(name) for arrays, and maybe(name) for a key that may be absent:

let info = ParsedPlist(bytes).dictionary();
info.text("CFBundleIdentifier");
info.date("Built");
info.maybe("LSUIElement").boolean() else false;

A missing key is MissingPlistMember; a value of another kind is PlistKindMismatch, which names the key and both kinds. No value is converted: an integer is not a real.
